emissions from the\\\\n[AWS Sustainability API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sustainability/latest/APIReference/Welcome.html)\\\\nare context.\\\\n\\\\n## \\\\u26a0\\\\ufe0f Critical \\\\u2014 read first\\\\n\\\\n- **Load each named file in full, at the step that names it**, with `read_skill_resource`.\\\\n  Never `distill` or summarize this skill or its files in their place, and never grade from memory.\\\\n- **If a load fails, say so.** Start the report with `\\\\u26a0\\\\ufe0f <file> could not be loaded: <verbatim\\\\n  error>`, do not replace its rules with general knowledge, and mark the practices that depend\\\\n  on it NEEDS HUMAN INPUT.\\\\n- **Emissions are context; Carbon for month M publishes by the 21st of M+1, so before the 21st the\\\\n  latest month can be two back. That is the normal one-month lag, not missing data.\\\\n- **Never invent a business output metric.** Use the Step 1 fallback and say which.\\\\n- **Grade all 29 practices.** Never mark one MET without evidence; use NEEDS HUMAN INPUT.\\\\n- **Read-only.** Never call `Modify*`, `Delete*`, `Terminate*` or `Create*`. Not for per-instance rightsizing (point to\\\\n[AWS Compute Optimizer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/what-is-compute-optimizer.html)),\\\\ncost reduction as the main goal, or incident-time analysis: there is no live carbon signal.\\\\n\\\\n## Workflow checklist\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Scope and business output metric\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Topology \\\\u2014 load [references/workload-model.md](references/workload-model.md)\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: Workload shape and triggers\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: Resource intensity inputs \\\\u2014 load [references/proxy-metrics.md](references/proxy-metrics.md)\\\\n- [ ] Step 5: Environmental impact data \\\\u2014 load [references/framing-and-attribution.md](references/framing-and-attribution.md),\\\\n  [references/emissions-collection.md](references/emissions-collection.md) and [references/emissions-api-reference.md](references/emissions-api-reference.md)\\\\n- [ ] Step 6: KPIs, emissions sanity check, cost\\\\u2013carbon divergence\\\\n- [ ] Step 7: Assess all 29 practices \\\\u2014 load [references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md](references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md)\\\\n- [ ] Step 8: Explain emissions changes\\\\n- [ ] Step 9: Report \\\\u2014 load [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md)\\\\n\\\\nDo not start a step before the previous one is done. Do not start Step 7 or Step 9 until its\\\\nfile is loaded.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 1 \\\\u2014 Scope and business output metric\\\\n\\\\nAsk for the scope (an entry point, application, set of accounts, or \\\\\"everything in this\\\\naccount\\\\\"; default: all configured Regions) and the business output metric \\\\u2014 the unit of work\\\\nthe workload produces. Over 30 days at `Period: 3600`, derive provisioned and\\\\nutilized vCPU-hours (vCPU \\\\u00d7 hours \\\\u00d7 utilization, never instance counts), weighted GB-months\\\\nand weighted GB transferred, and the business output for the same window. Record each\\\\nresource\\'s architecture (`x86_64` or `arm64`) and instance generation. The storage and\\\\nnetwork weights are directional, not a carbon model; say so in the report. For AI/ML, collect\\\\nthe inputs listed in `ai-ml-workloads.md`.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 5 \\\\u2014 Environmental impact data\\\\n\\\\nLoad [references/framing-and-attribution.md](references/framing-and-attribution.md) and [references/emissions-collection.md](references/emissions-collection.md), and\\\\nread [references/emissions-api-reference.md](references/emissions-api-reference.md) before the first call. More than one account returned is a\\\\n  management-account view: report per account and say so. Only this account is a member or\\\\n  standalone view. Never assert either without that evidence. Only EC2, S3 and CloudFront are\\\\n  broken out by service; the rest is \\\\\"Other\\\\\". `GetEstimatedCarbonEmissionsDimensionValues` is\\\\n  optional; if it fails, continue.\\\\n- Water: `GetEstimatedWaterAllocation`, `YEARLY_CALENDAR`, `Start` on 1 January. It is\\\\n  disclosure only: no Well-Architected practice or KPI is water-specific, so derive no finding,\\\\n  KPI, trend driver or recommendation from it, and never attribute a change in it to the\\\\n  customer. If asked how to reduce it, say in one sentence that the review\\'s resource-efficiency\\\\n  findings are the only levers; list no water actions.\\\\n  If the call fails or returns nothing, ask for a water export from the Sustainability console\\\\n  and load [references/csv-emissions-input.md](references/csv-emissions-input.md).\\\\n- Attempt carbon and water independently, record the `ModelVersion`, and handle every failure\\\\n  with the \\\\\"no data\\\\\" table in `emissions-collection.md`.\\\\n\\\\n### Step 6 \\\\u2014 KPIs and checks\\\\n\\\\nUse the KPI set in `proxy-metrics.md` that fits the shape: current value, 30 days prior,\\\\nchange, direction. Add the Graviton KPIs from `graviton-migration.md`, and report AI/ML KPIs\\\\nfrom `ai-ml-workloads.md` in a separate table. Then:\\\\n- **Emissions sanity check** \\\\u2014 compare emissions with the provisioned footprint using the\\\\n  tests in `proxy-metrics.md`. {"id": "904b7b30-f78a-4dc3-8f1c-9380e64274eb", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_tnWXhnk7okDFiGRkFZjfeF", "content": "[{'text': '# Carbon and Water CSV Exports\\n\\nRead this file at Step 5 when a carbon or water `.csv` export is attached or referenced, when\\nthe customer prefers to supply an export instead of granting API access, or when the water call\\nfails or returns nothing.\\n\\n## When to use a CSV export\\n\\nThe AWS Sustainability API is the default source. A CSV export is the supported alternative in\\ntwo cases:\\n\\n| Use | When | What the customer supplies |\\n|-----|------|----------------------------|\\n| Customer-supplied data | The customer prefers to supply their own export instead of granting the agent\\'s role the `sustainability:` actions, or attaches one | A carbon or water export from **Reports** in the AWS Sustainability console, or a carbon export from AWS Data Exports delivered as CSV. Neither needs a `sustainability:` action on the agent\\'s role. |\\n| Water fallback | `GetEstimatedWaterAllocation` fails, or returns no result | A water export from **Reports** in the AWS Sustainability console. Data Exports does not carry water data, so the console is the only export source for water. |\\n\\nIf the customer says they prefer to supply an export but has not attached one, ask for it before\\ncalling the API for that metric. When a carbon call fails, the \"no data\" table in\\n`references/emissions-collection.md` also offers this route.\\n\\n## Step 5: Resolve the route first\\n\\nCheck for an attached export before the first API call, then resolve each metric in this order.\\nDo not treat a carbon-only attachment as a reason to skip the water call, or the reverse.\\n\\n| Order | Route | Use when |\\n|-------|-------|----------|\\n| 1 | **Attached CSV** (Step 5.0) | A carbon or water `.csv` is attached, or the user references one. Use it for the metric it covers. |\\n| 2 | **AWS Sustainability API** (Steps 5.1, 5.2) | For every metric no attached CSV covers. |\\n| 3 | **Requested CSV** (Step 5.0) | The water call failed or returned nothing: ask the user for a console water export. If none is supplied, report water as unavailable. |\\n\\nIf both are available for the same metric, **prefer the attached CSV** \u2014 an explicit attachment\\nis a deliberate choice of input, and overriding it with the API silently discards what the user\\nsupplied. Still call the API for any metric the CSV does not cover. Never merge the two sources\\ninto one figure or table; report whichever you used and say which.\\n\\n### 5.0 Read and validate the export\\n\\nRead the file and map its columns rather than assuming a layout. A carbon export has one row per\\nperiod \u00d7 service \u00d7 Region (and per account, when the export carries an account column) and uses\\nthese column names:\\n\\n| Column | Meaning | Maps to |\\n|--------|---------|---------|\\n| `usage_year` or `usage_month` / `usage_period_start` | Reporting period | Determines granularity \u2014 see the granularity rule below |\\n| `service` or `product_code` | AWS service | `GroupBy: SERVICE` equivalent |\\n| `region` or `region_code` / `location` | Region (display name or code) | `GroupBy: REGION` equivalent |\\n| `usage_account_id` / `payer_account_id` | Account scope | Confirms whose data this is \u2014 reconcile against Step 1 |\\n| `total_lbm_emissions_value` | Location-based total, MTCO2e | `TOTAL_LBM_CARBON_EMISSIONS` |\\n| `total_mbm_emissions_value` | Market-based total, MTCO2e | `TOTAL_MBM_CARBON_EMISSIONS` |\\n| `total_scope_1_emissions_value` | Scope 1 | `TOTAL_SCOPE_1_CARBON_EMISSIONS` |\\n| `total_scope_2_lbm_emissions_value` / `total_scope_2_mbm_emissions_value` | Scope 2, both methods | `TOTAL_SCOPE_2_*_CARBON_EMISSIONS` |\\n| `total_scope_3_lbm_emissions_value` / `total_scope_3_mbm_emissions_value` | Scope 3, both methods | `TOTAL_SCOPE_3_*_CARBON_EMISSIONS` |\\n| `cfe_savings_value` | Carbon-free-energy benefit, = LBM \u2212 MBM | No API equivalent; report as-is, do not add to any total |\\n| `model_version` | Methodology version | `ModelVersion` \u2014 quote it exactly as it appears |\\n| `*_unit` columns, if present | Unit of the adjacent value | Verify it is `MTCO2e`.
